properties.name: Bridgewater Triangle & Hockomock Swamp
properties.subtitle: South-eastern Massachusetts, United States
properties.claim: A roughly 500 km² area of south-eastern Massachusetts said to concentrate UFO sightings, thunderbirds, Bigfoot reports, poltergeists and ritual sites — a terrestrial Bermuda Triangle named by cryptozoologist Loren Coleman in 1970.
properties.context: The 'triangle' is a modern framing drawn around a pre-existing folkloric landscape; Hockomock itself is a Wampanoag name often rendered 'place where spirits dwell'. The core is a large, genuinely difficult wetland that was a refuge during King Philip's War, which seeded centuries of local legend. No category of report here exceeds the regional baseline once population and reporting activity are accounted for.
properties.summary: The Bridgewater Triangle is an area of about 200 square miles (520 km2) within southeastern Massachusetts in the United States, claimed to be a site of alleged paranormal phenomena, ranging from UFOs to poltergeists, and other spectral phenomena, various bigfoot-like sightings, giant snakes and thunderbirds. The term was coined by New England-based cryptozoologist Loren Coleman.
properties.short_description: Area in Massachusetts claimed to be the site of paranormal phenomena
